display_name: Penal Code 1871 — six property and intimidation offences, s 301, and the form of a charge
versions_encoded: Penal Code 1871 as in force 17 September 2026 (2020 Revised Edition with amendments to Act 21 of 2025)
s 301 as substituted by Act 15 of 2019, in force 1 January 2020
scope: Sections 22–25 (property, wrongful gain and loss, dishonestly, fraudulently); 378–379 theft; 383–384 extortion; 390, 392, 393, 394 robbery; 405–406 criminal breach of trust; 415, 417, 420 cheating; 503, 506 criminal intimidation; 321, 323A hurt; 301 transferred malice. Each punishing section exports a charge builder that recites the charge in the form the Criminal Procedure Code 2010 ss 123–126 prescribe, or refuses with the elements not made out (CPC s 123(5)). Riders: s 34 common intention as a header clause only; no s 109 abetment, no CPC s 124(4) amalgamation, no general attempt under s 511 (s 393, which punishes an attempt at robbery specifically, IS encoded). Illustrations and Explanations are carried as comments and as @desc text, not as rules. The evidence layer (what a fact rests on) is app-side, not encoded.

validation.bench: seven reported cases whose charges are quoted verbatim in the judgment: Lewis Christine [2001] SGHC 113 (s 420), Sarjit Singh Rapati [2005] SGHC 28 (s 384 r/w 34), Chen Weixiong Jerriek [2003] SGHC 103 (s 392 r/w 34, s 394), Carl Elias Moses [1995] 3 SLR 748 as quoted in Viswanathan Ramachandran [2003] SGHC 183 (s 406, REFUSED as laid), Chan Yok Tuang [2008] SGHC 137 (s 506, REFUSED), Ang Boon Han [2024] SGHC 221 (s 323A); plus s 378 Illustration (q), s 390 Illustration (b), s 405 Illustrations (c)–(d), s 503 Illustration, s 323A Illustration
